chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: How much did Lester shape the Basie sound?
summary: Stanley Dance argues the Moten band already had the Basie principles, while Helen Dance stresses Lester.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, I mean -- it would seem to me that the world of music that the Basie band went into, and became identified with, was the one that Lester led them into.
The band probably wouldn't have got there, exactly. Well, I mean, Billy played her part, in that too, in a way.

I disagree with you a little bit there. I think you're overplaying that a little bit, because if you listen to that record of Benny Moten's band in 1932 -- you've got Basie in there, Walter Page, Lips Page and Ben Webster.
The principals of the later Basie band are all laid out for you there. I mean, you put Johnny Hodges in the Duke Ellington band -- now that makes a -- obviously that does something for Ellington.
And, I think to give -- I mean I'm not trying to take anything away from Lester, but I think you're overstressing --
Now wait -- what happens when he's gone? Sure -- I mean, you know, when you have all these other great tenor players. Now it isn't the same --
It isn't the same at all. But, nevertheless, I think that -- you know -- you might say that Charlie Parker was in Jay McShann's band. And, it didn't mean -- so everybody always --
when you'd talk of Joy McShann -- what they'd think of immediately is Charlie Parker. But Joy McShann's band is going to be the same with or without Charlie Parker.
